prize_parts.citation: For the discovery of gamma-ray burst afterglows and the establishment of the cosmological origin of gamma-ray bursts

statement.case_for: The localization of gamma-ray bursts by BeppoSAX, which delivered the X-ray afterglow of GRB 970228, and the optical, radio and redshift follow-up that placed the bursts at cosmological distances, resolved a puzzle that stood for about thirty years. This is a clue from nature, not an elegant idea awaiting confirmation. It turned a mystery into a field: bursts as the deaths of massive stars and as products of compact-object mergers, and as probes of the distant universe. More than a quarter of a century of confirmation by Swift, Fermi and other missions leaves the interpretation stable. The discovery has an existential dimension, since we now see stellar deaths from the early universe, and the committee has not recognised this chain of results.
statement.case_against: The attribution is the weak point. The decisive steps were taken by large teams and by instruments, and the optical counterpart and first redshift (van Paradijs, Djorgovski, Metzger and colleagues, with Kulkarni's group) do not map cleanly onto three names. I cannot be sure that every key contributor is eligible. Opening support is thin: only Mark Pearce and I ranked B038 at all, so it may be the least supported of the leading candidates. B018 has a far cleaner two-person credit and broader support, and my own case could fail on attribution alone.

responses.point: B038 is a decisive space-instrument result, mature and arguably late, but optical and redshift credit is contested and some key people may no longer be eligible.
responses.response: I agree with Mark that the credit is the real problem, and I also share his reading of the maturity. The cleanest line is X-ray localization (Costa, Frontera) plus the optical, radio and redshift programme that established the distance (Kulkarni). I would sooner accept an imperfect boundary than leave a thirty-year puzzle unrecognised, but I would want the committee to test that boundary against the record. I would not follow Mark's first choice, B007: the diffuse flux is well established, but three names cannot represent a collaboration of hundreds, and source identification still rests on a few associations.

responses.point: Optical lattice clocks are a new way of measuring time, with a clean two-name credit (Katori, Ye), independent confirmation and timely recognition.
responses.response: Stefan makes the strongest case on attribution and maturity, and I accept that B018 is the most defensible package on the list. My reservation is that the clock is a superb instrument whose headline payoffs, the redefinition of the second and relativistic geodesy, are still prospective, and it follows the 2005 frequency-comb and 2012 ion-control prizes. I do not think that is disqualifying, so I place B018 first among my alternatives. My view is that B038 has a larger discovery content and B018 has the cleaner credit.

responses.point: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene is a new platform for correlated matter, a clean pairing of prediction (Bistritzer, MacDonald) and experiment (Jarillo-Herrero), reproduced widely.
responses.response: Olle's account of the prediction-plus-experiment structure convinces me, and it is why I ranked B044 fourth. My caution is the one several of us noted: the pairing mechanism is unresolved, and the field is changing fast with moire TMDs and other platforms. Recognising a discovery whose interpretation is not stable is the opposite of what I look for. I would wait unless the committee concludes that the platform, not the mechanism, is the discovery.

responses.point: Circuit QED made strong light-matter coupling available on a chip and underlies superconducting processors, though the allocation among Blais, Girvin, Schoelkopf and Wallraff is unresolved and Göran declares proximity to the field.
responses.response: I value Göran's candour about his proximity, and the allocation problem he describes is real: four credited names for three places, with Girvin the painful omission. I worry more about timing. Following the 2025 circuit prize, a second superconducting-circuit award would need a clear argument that light-matter coupling is a distinct discovery and not engineering of the same platform. I have not heard that argument made yet.

uncertainties: Who exactly should share credit for the optical counterpart and redshift of the gamma-ray bursts, and whether the BeppoSAX instrument leadership is fairly captured by Costa and Frontera
Whether Kulkarni's follow-up should be the second prize part or whether the prize should be limited to the X-ray localization
Whether the committee wants a second precision-measurement prize (B018) after 2005 and 2012, which would push B038 and B004 to the fore
Whether the thin opening support for B038 can be strengthened by expert reports on attribution
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my provided profile for any shortlisted candidate. My string-theory and cosmology background and my dark-energy views are only remotely related to B004, where I have a scientific interest but no personal tie to the credited names.
